newsitem.title: USA: Calif. home sales surged in 1996 - report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. home sales surged in 1996 - report.

text.p: California existing home sales surged nearly 19 percent in 1996 to the highest levels since 1989, the California Association of Realtors reported on Tuesday.
Statewide, 505,220 existing, single-family, detached homes closed escrow during 1996, up 18.8 percent from 1995, when 425,390 homes were sold, the association said.
The statewide median price of an existing, single-family detached home was $177,630 in 1996, virtually unchanged from $178,160 in 1995, the association said.
The association said 44 percent of California households could afford to purchase the median-priced, detached home at the end of 1996, up from 40 percent at the end of 1995.

Closed-escrow sales of existing condominiums increased 29.2 percent in 1996, compared with the 1995 level. The statewide median condominium price edged down 0.7 percent from $137,150 in 1995 to $136,230 in 1996, the association said.
The association said 57 percent of California households could afford to purchase the median-priced condominium at the end of 1996, up from 53 percent at the end of 1995.

"As a result of advantageous interest rates, rising incomes and great housing buys, affordability has surged to new highs in this decade," California Association of Realtors President Bob Kulick said.
"We expect this positive affordability environment to drive additional increases in the California housing market in 1997," Kulick said.
